The output sits at 1.559 V, about 60 mV over the 1.5 V limit. Vout ≈ Vgs1 + Vsg_f, and both devices run near subthreshold, so making them wider pulls both voltages down by roughly 70–80 mV per decade of width. Shortening Lf also helps.

```json
{"action": "refine", "reason": "Only vout_dc fails (1.559 V vs 1.5 V). Vout = Vgs1 + Vsg_f, both near subthreshold, so wider W1 and Wf plus shorter Lf should cut 80-120 mV. Bandwidth (27 MHz) and noise margins allow the extra capacitance. Bounds widened to let the refiner reach these sizes.",
 "params": {"W1": 30.0, "L1": 0.3, "Wf": 50.0, "Lf": 0.15, "Rf": 560e3, "RL": 50e3},
 "bounds": {"W1": [8.0, 80.0], "Wf": [16.0, 120.0], "Lf": [0.15, 0.5], "L1": [0.15, 1.0]}}
```
